items.headline: Nonprofit Production Waterwell Doubles Funding for Unseen Iran Grants to Artists Representing the Diaspora in Film, TV, Theater and More
items.facts: Nonprofits Waterwell and Nimruz opened applications for the second cycle of Unseen Iran Grants and doubled the program's funding.

framing.narrativeTitle: Waterwell and Nimruz Expand Unseen Iran Grants
framing.publicBrief: Waterwell and Nimruz announce the second cycle of the Unseen Iran Grants, doubling the program’s funding to support artists of the Iranian diaspora working in film, TV, theater and related media. The call invites submissions that explore diaspora experiences, with the expanded budget allowing more projects to receive support. Arian Moayed, noted actor and advocate, highlights the grant’s role in amplifying under‑represented voices.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are an artist of the Iranian diaspora preparing a proposal that could receive funding from the expanded grant program.

howItWorks: Applicants submit project proposals to Waterwell and Nimruz during the open window.
The two nonprofits review submissions jointly and allocate the doubled funds across selected projects.
Funding is awarded only to proposals that meet the grant’s thematic criteria.
Unselected applicants receive feedback but no financial support.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: Submit your proposal or wait for the next cycle

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: Your proposal is funded, enabling production of a diaspora‑focused work.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: Your proposal is not selected, and you miss the current funding round.
outcomes.MIXED: Your proposal receives partial support, allowing limited development of the project.

framing.publicBrief: Waterwell and Nimruz have doubled the funding for the second cycle of Unseen Iran Grants, targeting artists of the Iranian diaspora in film, TV, and theater. Arian Moayed champions the initiative to amplify underrepresented voices. The expanded budget must be allocated between production resources and artist stipends. Waterwell controls the distribution ledger, while Nimruz holds the artistic mandate. The parties must agree on the split before the submission window closes.

roleFlavor.proposer: You represent Waterwell. You hold the pen that allocates the doubled funds. You decide the ratio of infrastructure support to direct artist payments.
roleFlavor.responder: You represent Nimruz. You hold the mandate to protect the artists. You can accept the proposed split or reject it, halting the disbursement entirely.

howItWorks: Waterwell proposes a division of the new grant funds.
Nimruz reviews the proposal and decides whether to accept.
If Nimruz accepts, the funds are distributed as proposed.
If Nimruz rejects, the entire grant cycle is paused.
missionCopy.choicePrompt: How will the doubled funds be divided?

outcomes.COOPERATIVE: The split is accepted and the grants are distributed.
outcomes.BETRAYAL: The proposal is rejected and the funds remain locked.
outcomes.MIXED: Negotiations stall as the deadline approaches.

items.headline: Wait, a Network Is Actually Suing the Trump Administration for Once?
items.facts: ABC sued the Trump administration alleging the FCC infringed on its First Amendment rights.

items.headline: Wetherspoons pubs ban playing music or taking calls on phone speakers
items.facts: Wetherspoons announced a ban on customers playing music or taking calls on speaker, asking them to use earphones or silent mode.

framing.publicBrief: Wetherspoons has announced that customers may no longer play music or take calls on speaker. Patrons must use earphones or silent mode. The bar has to enforce the rule while keeping guests satisfied.

roleFlavor.hunter: Wetherspoons must decide how strictly to enforce the new policy, risking customer frustration or a calm atmosphere.

framing.publicBrief: It is 2 AM in a Wetherspoons pub. The ban on phone speakers and loud music is in effect. Wetherspoons requires silence; customers want to talk. Everyone hears the same rule, but each person decides whether to obey based on what they think the rest of the room will do. If most people keep their voices down, the pub is calm. If many ignore the rule, the noise returns.

roleFlavor.guesser: You hold your phone. You can hear the ambient noise of the room. You must decide your own behavior before seeing what others choose.

items.headline: Tupac Shakur murder trial: gang leader plotted killing to avenge beating of nephew, court hears
items.facts: Duane “Keffe D” Davis is on trial for allegedly orchestrating the 1996 drive‑by shooting that killed Tupac Shakur in retaliation for an attack on his nephew.

framing.narrativeTitle: The Drive-by at the MGM Grand
framing.publicBrief: It is 3 AM outside the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. Traffic is gridlocked on Koval Lane. Inside a moving car, Tupac Shakur waits in the darkness. Somewhere in the stalled traffic, Duane “Keffe D” Davis watches. Davis is on trial for orchestrating the drive-by shooting that killed Shakur, allegedly to avenge an attack on his nephew. The street is a narrow channel of steel and glass. One side holds the path; the other holds the weapon. The night is still, but the tension is absolute. Davis must decide whether to pull the trigger or let the car pass. Shakur cannot see him. The outcome hangs on a single decision made in the dark.

roleFlavor.driver: You are in the vehicle. You hear the engine idle and the tires screech. You know the threat is real, but you cannot see who is aiming. You are waiting for a signal that never comes.

items.headline: Publicis Groupe, 3 Arts, Travis Kelce Launch Venture to Help Advertisers Strike Deals With College A
items.facts: Publicis Groupe, 3 Arts and Travis Kelce formed a joint venture to help advertisers partner with college athletes.

framing.narrativeTitle: Publicis, 3 Arts and Kelce’s College Athlete Deal Hub
framing.publicBrief: Publicis Groupe, 3 Arts and NFL star Travis Kelce announce a joint venture that offers advertisers a direct path to partner with college athletes. The three creators pool their media reach, creative expertise, and athlete connections to build a marketplace where brands can negotiate sponsorships without navigating individual school rules. Each side hopes the platform will attract high‑value contracts, boost their own revenue streams, and give athletes a new source of income, while advertisers seek authentic connections with youthful audiences.

roleFlavor.hunter: You sit on the board of the new venture, watching the first wave of brand proposals arrive. Your reputation and future earnings depend on whether the partners lock in deals together or go it alone.

framing.publicBrief: It is mid-morning in the market. Publicis Groupe, 3 Arts, and Travis Kelce have formed a joint venture. The goal is to help advertisers strike deals with college athletes. The venture combines media reach, creative expertise, and athlete connections. The parties aim to build a marketplace for sponsorships. They seek to bypass individual school rules. The stake is the volume and value of the contracts secured through this new hub.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are part of the venture. You must gauge the market's appetite for this new model. Your success depends on aligning your expectations with the collective outcome.

items.headline: UK retailers too slow to pass on fuel price falls, watchdog says
items.facts: The Competition and Markets Authority raised concerns about passive pricing strategies used by many petrol stations that delay passing wholesale price changes to consumers.

framing.narrativeTitle: CMA pressures stations on pump prices
framing.publicBrief: The Competition and Markets Authority says many petrol stations keep retail fuel prices high even after wholesale costs drop. The watchdog warns that the delay hurts consumers and may breach competition rules. The stations argue they need time to adjust margins and cover operational costs. Both sides watch the market closely as price changes ripple through the supply chain.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are the regulator tasked with ensuring fair pricing, but you risk industry pushback if you force rapid cuts.

framing.publicBrief: Evening light fades over the forecourts. The Competition and Markets Authority has flagged a pattern: petrol stations are slow to pass wholesale fuel price falls to consumers. Stations hold the line, citing margin protection and operational costs. The watchdog warns this delay breaches competition norms. The market is static, each station watching the others to see who will blink first and cut prices.

items.headline: Reach Capital raises $265M Fund V to back AI founders building to ‘expand human potential’
items.facts: Reach Capital announced a $265 million Fund V to invest $1‑10 million in AI startups.

framing.publicBrief: Reach Capital has announced Fund V, a $265 million vehicle dedicated to backing AI founders. The fund targets early-stage companies, offering between $1 million and $10 million per investment to support ventures aiming to expand human potential. The capital is ready, but the terms of entry remain to be set between the firm and the entrepreneurs seeking it.

roleFlavor.proposer: You control the capital allocation for Fund V. You set the valuation and terms for the $1-$10 million checks.
roleFlavor.responder: You are an AI founder seeking capital. You must decide whether to accept the terms offered by Reach Capital.

items.headline: 270,000 Square Miles Around Easter Island to Become Indigenous-Managed Ocean Reserve
items.facts: Indigenous people of Easter Island will hold majority voting power on a sea council governing a large marine reserve, sharing seats with Chilean officials.

framing.publicBrief: It is late afternoon on Easter Island. The wind off the Pacific carries the smell of salt and diesel. A new sea council is being formed to govern 270,000 square miles of ocean. Indigenous people of Easter Island will hold majority voting power on this body, sharing seats with Chilean officials. The reserve is established, but the power to direct its management is now split between local heritage and state authority. The council meets to decide how the waters are managed.

roleFlavor.contributor: You represent the Indigenous people of Easter Island. You hold the majority vote on the sea council. Your authority is rooted in centuries of stewardship, but it must now be exercised within a formal

framing.publicBrief: The Indigenous people of Easter Island present a proposal to Chilean officials: they demand that fishing quotas in the newly declared marine reserve be reduced by 50% to protect local species. Chilean officials must decide whether to accept the cut, keeping current quotas, or reject it and maintain the status quo. The decision will shape the future of the island’s fishing economy and its ecological balance.

roleFlavor.proposer: You represent the Indigenous people of Easter Island, holding a strong claim to protect marine life and sustain community livelihoods. You risk losing political influence if the proposal is rejected.
roleFlavor.responder: You are a Chilean official responsible for national resource management. You can preserve current economic benefits for the region or cede control to local demands.

items.headline: Einride strikes deal to add 500 Tesla Semis to its fleet
items.facts: Einride will buy 500 Tesla Semis to add to its fleet, making them available to Amazon and other customers.

framing.narrativeTitle: Einride Expands Fleet with Tesla Semis
framing.publicBrief: At dawn, Einride announces a purchase of 500 Tesla electric semitrailers, adding them to its autonomous freight fleet. The vehicles will be offered to Amazon and other logistics customers, promising lower emissions and faster delivery times. Tesla gains a large order that boosts its commercial vehicle division, while Amazon secures a steady supply of zero‑emission trucks for its growing network. Both companies stand to benefit from the partnership, but the scale of the deal puts pressure on Einride to integrate the new units quickly.

roleFlavor.proposer: Einride holds the contract and must decide how to allocate the new trucks among its clients.
roleFlavor.responder: Tesla controls the production schedule and can choose how many units to prioritize for Einride versus other buyers.

items.headline: Johnny Depp in talks to return to Pirates of the Caribbean franchise
items.facts: Johnny Depp is in talks with producer Jerry Bruckheimer to return as Captain Jack Sparrow for a sixth Pirates of the Caribbean film.

framing.narrativeTitle: Depp and Bruckheimer: The Sixth Film
framing.publicBrief: Dawn breaks over the studio lot as Johnny Depp enters talks with producer Jerry Bruckheimer. The subject is a return to the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise for a sixth film. Bruckheimer holds the production rights and the greenlight; Depp holds the likeness of Captain Jack Sparrow. The project cannot proceed without the actor, but the actor needs the producer’s platform. They are negotiating the terms of this reunion in the quiet hours before the press cycle begins.

roleFlavor.proposer: You are Jerry Bruckheimer. You control the production budget and the distribution deal. You need Depp to make the film viable.
roleFlavor.responder: You are Johnny Depp. You hold the iconic role of Captain Jack Sparrow. Without your participation, the sixth film loses its anchor.

items.headline: Detroit startup Grounded raises $5M to customize electric and gas-powered vans
items.facts: Grounded shifted to customizing vans for small businesses after GM stopped BrightDrop and Ford cancelled its electric Transit plans.

framing.narrativeTitle: Grounded pivots as automakers pull back
framing.publicBrief: Grounded, a Detroit startup, announces a $5 million raise to turn its vans into custom work vehicles for small businesses. The move follows General Motors ending its BrightDrop program and Ford cancelling its electric Transit project, leaving a gap in the market for adaptable commercial transport. Grounded hopes the new funding lets it scale production while filling the void left by the two automakers.

framing.publicBrief: Grounded, a Detroit startup, secures $5 million to customize vans for small businesses. The funding arrives as General Motors stops BrightDrop and Ford cancels its electric Transit plans. With major manufacturers pulling back, Grounded aims to scale production of adaptable commercial vehicles. The company must decide how to position its customized fleet in a market suddenly reshaped by the exit of industry giants. The focus is on turning standard vans into specialized work vehicles that meet the immediate needs of local enterprises.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are a Grounded executive assessing the market void left by Ford and General Motors. You must determine the optimal volume and type of custom vans to produce, anticipating the needs of small busine

items.headline: ‘We detected unusual activity’: the scam that uses AI to exploit your holiday photos
items.facts: Fraudsters use travelers' Instagram photos to send phishing texts claiming unusual activity and lure victims to reveal bank details.

framing.publicBrief: It is 2 PM on a Tuesday. Instagram users are scrolling through their feeds, looking at photos from their recent holidays. Suddenly, their phones buzz. A text message arrives from a number they do not recognize. The message claims that Fraudsters have detected unusual activity on their accounts. It asks them to reply with bank details to secure their funds. The users must decide whether to trust the alert or ignore it. The Fraudsters wait for a response to complete the scam.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are an Instagram user. You hold your phone. You see the alert. You know you just posted holiday photos. You wonder if this is real.

framing.publicBrief: It is 2 PM on a Tuesday. Instagram users scroll through holiday photos when a text from an unknown number claims Fraudsters have spotted unusual activity on their accounts. The message urges them to reply with bank details to secure their funds. The users must decide whether to trust the alert or ignore it. The Fraudsters wait for a response to complete the scam.

roleFlavor.hunter: You are an Instagram user who just posted a beach photo. A text warns of suspicious activity on your account and asks for bank details to prevent a loss.

items.headline: Croatian Crime Drama ‘Red Water,’ Directed by Cannes Prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic, to Be
items.facts: Beta Film teamed up with ZDF/Arte and Antitalent to co‑produce the Croatian drama “Red Water.”

framing.publicBrief: At a bright early‑morning meeting in a repurposed factory loft, Beta Film, ZDF/Arte and Antitalent sit around a table. The three companies have just signed an exclusive agreement to co‑produce the Croatian crime drama ‘Red Water,’ directed by Cannes prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic. Each party will contribute funding, distribution channels and talent, and each hopes the series will boost its profile and revenue in European markets. The deal hinges on everyone honoring their commitments as the production moves into shooting.

roleFlavor.contributor: You are the coalition of Beta Film, ZDF/Arte and Antitalent, each holding a share of the financing and distribution plan and watching the others' contributions closely.

framing.publicBrief: The sun rises over the Adriatic coast as the final terms for the Croatian crime drama ‘Red Water’ are settled. Directed by Cannes prizewinner Antoneta Alamat Kusijanovic, the project requires a unified front. Beta Film, ZDF/Arte, and Antitalent must align their resources. The script is locked, the cast is waiting, and the distribution rights hang in the balance. One party holds the leverage to greenlight the shoot; the other must decide whether to accept the terms or walk away from the set entirely.

roleFlavor.proposer: You hold the distribution leverage. You set the terms for the co-production. If the other side refuses, the project stalls, and your investment sits idle.
roleFlavor.responder: You hold the creative assets and local access. You must decide if the deal offered by the financiers is worth your talent and time, or if you should walk away.

items.headline: Can festivals leave the land better than they found it?
items.facts: Festival organisers offered live recycling workshops while attendees brought plastic waste to be processed.

framing.narrativeTitle: Festival Organisers and Attendees: A Plastic Swap
framing.publicBrief: Festival organisers set up live recycling workshops on the grounds, inviting festival attendees to bring their plastic waste for processing. The organisers aim to clean the site and showcase sustainability, while attendees hope to learn and dispose of trash responsibly. The event promises a cleaner festival area for everyone.

items.headline: Sundance Breakout ‘Thelma’ Set for Mandarin Remake by Stars Collective, Titled ‘Grandma, Please’ (EX
items.facts: Stars Collective acquired the Mandarin-language remake rights to the Sundance film “Thelma.”

framing.publicBrief: Stars Collective announces it has secured the Mandarin-language remake rights to the Sundance breakout ‘Thelma.’ The rights holders have agreed to transfer the property, opening a path for a new version titled ‘Grandma, Please.’ Both parties stand to benefit: Stars Collective can tap the Chinese market, while the original owners receive a licensing fee and broader exposure for the story.

roleFlavor.proposer: Stars Collective holds the financing and production plan for the Mandarin version, ready to launch a major release in China.
roleFlavor.responder: The rights holders control the original intellectual property and must decide whether the offered terms reflect the film’s value.

items.headline: AI automation startup Relay shuts down, staff joins Google’s Chrome team
items.facts: Relay announced it is shutting down and some staff, including its CEO, are joining Google’s Chrome team.

framing.narrativeTitle: Relay Shuts Down, Staff Joins Google
framing.publicBrief: Relay has announced its immediate shutdown. At the same time, a group of its staff, including its CEO, are joining Google’s Chrome team. The decision marks the end of one venture and the beginning of another within the tech ecosystem. The move consolidates talent and resources under Google’s umbrella, ending the independent operations of Relay.

roleFlavor.guesser: You are a Relay employee deciding how to frame the move to Google.

items.headline: Anthropic’s annualized revenue surges to $65B
items.facts: Anthropic reported annualized revenue of $65 billion, up from $47 billion in May, and investors expect continued growth.

items.headline: Water companies in England and Wales explore ‘surge pricing’ during drought
items.facts: Water companies in England and Wales could be allowed to raise bills during drought periods under Ofwat proposals linking charges to water scarcity.
